items.text: A bar use at 995 Valencia requires Conditional Use Authorization and a Type 42 license transferred from another bar in the Mission SUD; high license density, a pattern of withdrawn bar CUAs nearby, and ABC's likely PCN requirement create substantial timeline and approval risk.
Planning Code §762 (NCT-Valencia zoning control table) classifies bar as a conditional use (C) on the first story; restaurant is principally permitted (P).

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§249.60) requires a new or relocated bar to use a liquor license transferred from another bar already within the SUD, not purchased new or transferred from outside the district.
An active ABC Type 41 eating-place license for Sarita's Grill & Beer was approved at 995 Valencia in November 2023; changing to a Type 42 bar license is a change of use requiring CUA.

Only N = 3 dated use decisions for bar or similar concepts were recorded within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years: 1 approved, 0 approved with conditions, 0 denied, 2 withdrawn; too few to calculate an approval rate.

A CUA for a bar within a full-service restaurant at 970-974 Valencia (66 m away, NCT-Valencia) was withdrawn in 2011 after five months without a hearing, and a CUA for a restaurant with Type 41 and live entertainment at 2519 Mission (210 m) was withdrawn in 2019 after three months.

The withdrawn bar CUAs in the Valencia corridor suggest applicants could not satisfy the Mission SUD transfer requirement, the ABC Public Convenience or Necessity process, or anticipated conditions at hearing.

Nine active ABC on-sale licenses exist within 500 ft and 51 within 1,000 ft of 995 Valencia; this density flags likely undue concentration under ABC rules, requiring a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city.

ABC Type 42 is a non-quota license, so new licenses are issued directly by ABC without a drawing, but the application requires a signed lease, a Planning zoning sign-off (the CUA), a 30-day posted notice, and a seller's permit.

Undue-concentration census tracts require a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors or Planning Commission; this process adds 1–3 months to the ABC timeline and introduces a second discretionary hearing.

Planning referrals for ABC Type 41 licenses at nearby restaurants (e.g., 1007 Valencia, 990 Valencia) were approved as continuations of restaurant use without triggering bar-use CUA, confirming that Type 41 is principally permitted but Type 42 is not.

The Mission SUD rule requiring a transferred Type 42 license means the applicant must locate and escrow a license from another bar within the SUD before ABC will accept the application; if no seller is found the project cannot proceed as a bar.

Live performance and amplified sound as a primary or ongoing use that runs until 1 am require a Place of Entertainment permit from the Entertainment Commission, with a $2,708 application fee (2026–27), Police and Planning referrals, and a Commission hearing.

Active POE permits are on file at Amados (998 Valencia, 31 m), Hidden Frequency (2500 Mission, 144 m), Arcana (2512 Mission, 150 m), and Foreign Cinema (2534 Mission, 172 m), demonstrating that the Entertainment Commission approves live entertainment in this corridor.

Planning approved the POE permit for Amados at 998 Valencia as accessory to an existing retail use, capping entertainment at one-third of gross floor area per Police Code §1060(r); a bar use with entertainment as primary may not qualify for that accessory route.

A recent nightclub use at 2500 Mission (145 m, NCT-Mission) was approved with one condition: adherence to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, which typically includes a community liaison, sound monitoring, and hours limits.

The POE permit application cannot be filed until the CUA is approved or a temporary liquor license is in place; Planning's zoning sign-off is a prerequisite for the Entertainment Commission intake meeting.

Any food facility with a kitchen (limited or full cooking) needs a DPH plan check ($828–$2,207 depending on scope, 2026–27) and a Permit to Operate ($470 application fee, 2026–27) after a final pre-opening inspection confirms the space matches approved plans.

The current ABC Type 41 license for Sarita's Grill & Beer at 995 Valencia indicates a food facility is already on file; DPH will review the scope of the new limited-cooking equipment and any changes to the existing hood, sinks, and finishes.

At least one owner or employee must hold a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate within 60 days of opening (CalCode §113947.1), and all food-handling employees must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire.

DPH agency referrals for restaurant health permits at nearby addresses (e.g., 990 Valencia, 1007 Valencia, 1014 Valencia) were approved as continuations of existing restaurant use, confirming that health permits are issued over the counter when the use and equipment do not change materially.

Tenant improvements including kitchen equipment, a hood, plumbing, electrical, and interior finishes require a building permit from DBI; a change of use from restaurant to bar triggers a Planning routing station and Section 311/312 neighborhood notification.

A change of use from an ABC Type 41 eating place (restaurant) to a Type 42 bar is a change of use under Planning Code §102 even though both serve alcohol, because restaurant and bar are distinct use categories with different zoning permissions.

The building permit will be held at the Planning routing station until the CUA is approved and the approval motion is final (after the 30-day appeal period); DBI will not issue the permit for a conditional use before Planning's decision is effective.

Limited cooking (panini press, small plates, charcuterie) typically requires a Type I commercial hood if it produces grease-laden vapor; SFPUC will assign a Fats, Oils & Grease discharger category and may require a grease interceptor or clarifier.

Expected condition: Hours of alcohol service limited to 6 am–2 am (state law); hours of operation (food and non-alcoholic service) may be limited to 6 am–1 am or midnight to align with nearby POE permits. Basis: Planning Code §762 permits operation 6 am–2 am as of right in NCT-Valencia; the concept proposes a 1 am close, which falls within that window. Active POE permits nearby (Amados, Arcana) do not have extracted closing-hour conditions, but the Entertainment Commission typically caps shows at 11 pm or midnight for venues on residential blocks.

Expected condition: Adherence to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, including appointment of a community liaison, a written sound-management plan, and participation in quarterly neighborhood meetings. Basis: The recent nightclub approval at 2500 Mission (2026-006164PRL) imposed one condition: adherence to the Good Neighbor Policy. This is standard for all POE permits and is explicitly mentioned in the Entertainment Commission's intake materials.

Expected condition: Live entertainment area limited to one-third of gross floor area if the bar use is approved with entertainment as an accessory use rather than a primary nighttime-entertainment use. Basis: Planning approved the POE permit for Amados at 998 Valencia with an explicit one-third floor-area cap per Police Code §1060(r) because entertainment was accessory to retail. If the CUA approves the bar use with entertainment as primary, this cap may not apply, but Planning may still condition the entertainment-area size.

Expected condition: Security plan including trained security staff on nights with live entertainment, ID checks at entry, and a procedure for refusing service to intoxicated patrons, as required by ABC and the Entertainment Commission. Basis: ABC's Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training mandate and the Entertainment Commission's standard operating conditions for POE permits both require written security and patron-management plans. Comparable POE permits do not have extracted security conditions, but the Commission's intake checklist requires the plan before the hearing.

Expected condition: Type 42 license restricted to beer and wine only; no spirits service permitted under this license type. Basis: ABC Type 42 is defined as on-sale beer and wine for public premises (bars) with no food requirement. The license does not authorize distilled spirits. The concept specifies beer-and-wine service, so this is a constraint of the chosen license type, not a discretionary condition.

Expected condition: Prohibition on dancing by patrons; live music and amplified sound permitted under the POE permit, but a dance floor or dancing as a primary activity would require a different use classification and likely additional conditions. Basis: The concept profile states dancing = false. Planning Code §102 classifies dance halls, discotheques, and nightclubs separately from bars and live-music venues. If patrons dance spontaneously, Planning may re-classify the use and require amendment of the CUA.

Expected condition: Compliance with SF's Fats, Oils & Grease ordinance: installation of a grease interceptor or clarifier if required by SFPUC, and filing of an Installation Verification Form to earn a sewer-bill discount. Basis: The SF FOG ordinance applies to all food service establishments that cook. SFPUC assigns a discharger category (1–3) based on the menu and cooking equipment; limited cooking (panini, small plates) typically falls into Category 2 or 3, requiring a passive grease interceptor.

Filing step: Engage a California ABC license broker to search for an available Type 42 (beer-and-wine bar) license being sold or transferred by another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, and negotiate a purchase agreement or letter of intent. What to say: Explain to the broker that the Mission SUD rule (Planning Code §249.60) prohibits a new bar from using a license transferred from outside the SUD or purchased new from ABC. Ask the broker to confirm that the seller's current premises is within the SUD boundary (roughly 16th to Cesar Chavez, Mission to Potrero) and that the license is a Type 42, not a Type 41 or 47. Secure a letter of intent or escrow agreement contingent on CUA and ABC approval; the lease should also be contingent on obtaining the license transfer.

Filing step: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State, obtain an EIN from the IRS, and register for a San Francisco Business Account Number (BAN) with the Treasurer & Tax Collector. What to say: File the entity formation first because the EIN, seller's permit, business registration, and ABC application all require the legal entity name. Use the same entity name on the lease. Register the business with SF within 30 days of forming the entity; the BAN is required for every other city permit (Planning, DPH, Entertainment Commission, DBI). The business registration fee is tiered by projected gross receipts; estimate conservatively to avoid a mid-year adjustment.

Filing step: Request a pre-application meeting with SF Planning to present the concept (bar use, live entertainment, 1 am close, limited cooking) and confirm the CUA filing requirements, the Mission SUD transfer rule, and likely conditions. What to say: Frame the concept as a neighborhood wine bar with a limited food menu and occasional live music (not a nightclub or late-night venue). Confirm that the CUA will address both the bar use (Planning Code §762, conditional in NCT-Valencia) and the Mission SUD transfer requirement (§249.60). Ask what operating conditions (hours, sound limits, security) Planning expects to see in the application, and whether a Good Neighbor outreach plan or letters of support from adjacent businesses will strengthen the case. Request written confirmation that a Type 42 license transferred from within the SUD satisfies the SUD rule.

Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including the project description, operating plan, proof of the Type 42 license purchase agreement, a Good Neighbor outreach summary, and the $3,100+ application fee. What to say: In the project narrative, emphasize that the concept is a bona fide eating place (limited cooking, table service) with beer-and-wine service accessory to the food menu, not a standalone bar. State that live entertainment will be limited to acoustic or small-ensemble performances ending by 11 pm or midnight (well before the 1 am close), and that the entertainment area will occupy no more than one-third of the floor area. Attach the Type 42 license purchase agreement or letter of intent showing the seller's premises is within the Mission SUD, and include a letter from the broker confirming the license is transferable. Describe outreach to neighbors and the Valencia Corridor Merchants Associat…

Filing step: After Planning posts the 300-foot mailed notice and the on-site posted notice, conduct additional outreach to recipients who may have concerns, and attend the Planning Commission hearing to present the concept and answer questions. What to say: At the hearing, reiterate that the bar use will be subordinate to the food service, that live entertainment will be low-intensity and end early, and that the applicant commits to all standard conditions (hours, sound monitoring, Good Neighbor Policy, no expansion of the license footprint). If neighbors or commissioners raise concerns about late-night noise or patron behavior, offer additional voluntary conditions: a 15-minute last-call announcement, a designated smoking area away from residential entries, or a written agreement to cap live-music nights at three per week. Do not argue against conditions; accept them and request approval.

Filing step: Once the CUA is approved and the 30-day appeal period has expired (making the approval effective), file the ABC Type 42 transfer application with the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control, including the CUA approval motion, the lease, the seller's permit, and the $1,000–$1,600 filing fee. What to say: Submit the ABC application online through the ABC Licensing Portal. Attach the final CUA motion as proof of local zoning approval, and reference Planning Code §249.60 and the Mission SUD in the cover letter to show the transfer satisfies the local ordinance. Post the ABC public notice at the premises for 30 days. Because the density statistics flag likely undue concentration (9 on-sale licenses within 500 ft), expect ABC to request a Public Convenience or Necessity finding; coordinate with Planning to prepare a PCN recommendation letter to the Board of Supervisors stating that the bar serves a neighborhood need and will operate responsibly.

Filing step: File the Place of Entertainment permit application with the SF Entertainment Commission, including the approved CUA motion, the POE application fee ($2,708 for 2026–27), a detailed sound-management plan, and a Good Neighbor operating agreement. What to say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director before filing to confirm zoning eligibility and POE category (the bar use is now approved via CUA, so the POE is approvable). In the application, describe the live entertainment as occasional acoustic or small-ensemble performances (solo guitar, duo, small jazz trio) in a designated 200 sq ft area, ending by 11 pm on weeknights and midnight on weekends. Attach a sound-management plan that commits to a sound limiter on the PA system, acoustic treatment on walls adjacent to residential units, and a community liaison who will receive and respond to noise complaints within 24 hours. Post the yellow Entertainment Commission notice for 30 days an…

Filing step: File the DPH health plan check and the DBI building permit application (with Health, Planning, Fire, and PUC routing) for the tenant improvements, showing the limited-cooking equipment, hood, sinks, and finishes. What to say: Submit the DPH plan check and the DBI application in parallel, ideally after the CUA is approved so Planning's routing station clears quickly. The building-permit plans should show the kitchen layout (panini press or small oven, three-compartment sink, hand-wash sink, prep surfaces), a Type I commercial hood if cooking produces grease-laden vapor, the bar area with beer taps and a small wine cooler, the 40-seat dining area, and the ~200 sq ft entertainment area. The DPH plan check should include a menu describing limited cooking (panini, charcuterie, small plates). Note on the plans that the existing Type 41 food facility will be modified but the use is now a bar (Type 42) per the approved…

Entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (bar use + Mission SUD compliance) → ABC Type 42 transfer with PCN finding → Place of Entertainment permit → Building permit + Health permit for tenant improvements. Estimated time: 365 to 730 days. Estimated government cost: $9,500 to $28,000. Notes: The critical path is the CUA for bar use, which takes 4–10 months (120–300 days per the catalog) including pre-application meetings, filing, environmental review, 300-foot notification, the hearing, and the 30-day appeal period. The ABC Type 42 transfer adds 60–150 days per the catalog, but in an undue-concentration tract with a PCN requirement the timeline stretches to 90–180 days because the Board of Supervisors PCN referral adds 1–3 months. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days per the catalog) can be filed after the CUA is approved; it runs in parallel with the building permit but is a prerequisite for the final Certificate of Occupancy, so it is on the critical path. The building permit for tenant improvements takes 14–120 days depending on plan complexity and whether DBI routes to multiple departments; with a CUA already approved, Planning's routing station should clear in 2–4 weeks. Health plan check and final inspection add 21–60 days and usually run in parallel with the building permit. Government fees: CUA $3,100–$15,000 (lower end for a no-construction use change, higher if tenant improvements are included in the application), ABC transfer $1,000–$1,600, POE permit $2,708, DPH plan check $828–$2,207, Health Permit to Operate $470, building permit $800–$15,000 (depending on construction valuation), plus state and federal registrations (entity $70–$150, EIN $0, business registration $55–$700, seller's permit $0). Total hard costs (excluding the Type 42 license purchase price, which can range from $15,000 to $80,000+ depending on market availability): $9,500–$28,000. The timeline assumes no appeals, no discretionary review, and no major plan revisions; an appeal of the CUA or POE permit adds 3–6 months. The biggest uncertainty is the availability of a Type 42 license for transfer within the Mission SUD; if none is available, the project cannot proceed as a bar and must pivot to a restaurant (Type 41, principally permitted) or wait indefinitely for a license to come to market.
